html:
A high-speed railway in western Saudi Arabia, opened in 2018, that links the two holy cities of Islam, Mecca and Medina, by way of Jeddah. Haramain means "the two sanctuaries".

The line is about 450 kilometres long, and trains run at up to 300 kilometres an hour, so the trip between the two cities takes some two and a half hours instead of many hours by road. A Spanish group of companies built the track and supplied the trains, which had to cope with heat and desert sand.

It was built to carry millions of pilgrims during the Hajj and the year-round lesser pilgrimage, as Saudi Arabia plans for ever more visitors. A century earlier the Ottomans had built the Hejaz Railway to bring pilgrims to Medina, which was wrecked in World War I and never reached Mecca.
